title: Regional routing circuit breakers and chaos-probe notes
content:
Status: DRAFT / working notes (not yet final ops playbook)

Overview
--------
Purpose: capture a compact design + embedded operational runbook for region-level circuit breakers and the lightweight chaos probe strategy we run from the control plane. Goal is to give on-call SREs and platform engineers a short, actionable reference for detecting, containing, and recovering region routing/control-plane incidents without excessive manual coordination.

Context / motivation
--------------------
- We operate multi-region clusters with smart routing: traffic is assigned by preference (region affinity), cost tier, and latency policy.
- Recent incidents (see PLAT-1021) showed that partial regional degradation (e.g., P99 spikes + increased 5xx) can silently spike cost and token queues if routing continues to push traffic into the degraded region.
- Introduce region-level circuit breakers with automated probes so that the router can fast-fail to healthy regions and avoid cascading overload.

High-level design summary
-------------------------
- Circuit-breaker abstraction lives in the control plane routing component (route-proxy-service).
- Per-region breaker state: CLOSED | OPEN | PROBING (half-open) managed with sliding windows (60s / 5m).
- Triggers: error-rate (% 5xx / gRPC errors), p99 latency, queue backlog, and API-level throttling responses from region. Each metric has a primary threshold and a secondary escalation threshold.
- Safe-fallback policy: when region X breaker opens, routing % to X is reduced by incremental steps (fast path: immediate soft-fail 80% of non-affine traffic; conservative path: shift only new requests).
- Chaos probes: lightweight synthetic request runner from control plane to each region every 30s when in PROBING or once every 5m in steady state. Probes exercise small token-length generation and embedding endpoints to check both RPC path and model runtime health.

State machine & thresholds (living defaults)
--------------------------------------------
- CLOSED: normal routing.
- PROBING (half-open): after OPEN for min_open_seconds (default 60s), send N probes (3) over probe_window (30s). If success_rate >= 75% and p99 probe latency < 2x baseline, transition to CLOSED; else return to OPEN.
- OPEN: initial trigger (example): 5xx_rate > 3% over 60s AND p99 > baseline * 2.5 OR queue_depth > 75% of capacity for two consecutive 30s windows. Escalation opens faster if health endpoint responding but runtimes returning errors.

Metric mapping (where to look)
-------------------------------
- dashboards/platform/region-health (Grafana) => panels: region_error_rate_60s, region_p99_latency_60s, region_queue_depth, model_runtime_errors.
- logging: routing-proxy logs (kubectl logs -l app=routing-proxy -n platform) filter by region tag.
- traces: controlplane-request-id traces in Jaeger for failed probes.

Operational runbook (incident flow)
-----------------------------------
1) Alerting (automatic):
   - Pager triggers when any region_error_rate_60s > 3% OR region_p99_latency_60s > baseline * 2.5 OR region_queue_depth > 75%.
   - Pager receiver: platform-sre oncall.

2) Initial triage (first 5–10 minutes):
   - Check Grafana region-health and model-runtime panels (link above). Confirm whether the signal is isolated to one region or multiple.
   - Run an ad-hoc probe from control plane:
       redwoodctl probe region --region=eu-west-1 --type=small-gen
     - Expected: 200 + sample tokens in < 600ms baseline for small-gen models.
   - Inspect routing-proxy logs for spike patterns:
       kubectl -n platform logs deployment/routing-proxy --since=15m | grep eu-west-1 | tail -n 200
   - Check slow downstream dependencies (eg. object storage, registry) referenced in region health.

3) Containment (if region confirmed degraded)
   - Option A: Flip region circuit breaker to OPEN (recommended for clear 5xx flood)
       # dry-run first to see estimated route delta
       redwoodctl route simulate --region eu-west-1 --action open-cb
       # apply change
       redwoodctl route apply --region eu-west-1 --action open-cb --reason "auto/oncall: spike 5xx"

     - Behavior: routing-proxy will drain new affinity-less traffic and reduce region share by configured percent (default 80% of best-effort traffic). Affinity-preserving sessions are honored for short TTL (to avoid UX breaks).

   - Option B: Soft-throttle (for noisy latency but not failing)
       redwoodctl route adjust --region eu-west-1 --throttle 0.5 --reason "soft-throttle p99 spike"

   - If the control plane UI is unreachable, use the emergency API (internal) to set breaker state:
       curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/regions/eu-west-1/breaker" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRLPLANE_TOKEN" -d '{"state":"open","reason":"oncall manual"}'

4) Recovery & validation (PROBING)
   - After containment, wait minimum open period (default 60s) then start PROBING. Probes run automatically; oncall should monitor probe success rate.
   - Manual probe: redwoodctl probe region --region=eu-west-1 --runs 6 --type=small-gen --log
   - If probes meet criteria -> allow closed transition OR manually set to CLOSED with note.
   - If probes fail: investigate region-level infra (node health, autoscaler throttles, infra quotas) and engage infra team.

5) Rollback criteria (when to revert breaker changes)
   - p99 latency and 5xx rate within 20% of baseline for 5 consecutive minutes (or 10m for conservative).
   - Model runtime metrics show healthy threads and memory.
   - No queue backlog.

6) Escalation matrix
   - Platform SRE oncall (primary) — page 1.
   - Platform lead (Sofia Reed) — if >30m impact or cross-region propagation.
   - Serving runtime lead (Daniel Park) — for model runtime errors or poor probe responses.
   - Customer success for high customer impact or SLA risk.

7) Safer manual operations checklist (for oncall)
   - Announce intent on #platform-ops with short summary and link to incident pager.
   - Run a simulator command to preview traffic shift (redwoodctl route simulate ...).
   - Apply change; monitor for 60s; if downstream region sees overload, revert within 5m.
   - Record exact commands and reasons in the incident channel (copy to postmortem later).

Chaos probing notes (running experiments without causing customer impact)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Controlled chaos probes: run low-volume synthetic traffic that does not count against customer quotas. Probes are labeled as synthetic and low-priority so they never evict customer requests.
- Frequency: default steady-state 1 probe / region / 5m. If region is in PROBING state, escalate to 3 probes / 30s.
- Probe types: small-gen (short token generation), embedding (single embedding), health-only (k/v × health-check).
- Failure modes: probes fail but production might still be healthy (false positive). To reduce noise, we require >=2 metric signals (e.g., p99 + increased 5xx) before auto-opening breaker.

Telemetry and observability action items (TODO)
----------------------------------------------
- Add a Grafana panel that overlays probe success rate over production p99 for each region (PLAT-1021).
- Add alert route for synthetic probe flapping separate from customer-facing error alerts.
- Instrument routing-proxy to emit reason-code when it routes around an OPEN region (so we can attribute cost savings).

Post-incident / runbook hygiene
------------------------------
- After an incident, create a short postmortem: timeline, root cause, corrective actions, follow-ups. Attach to PLAT-1021 (example).
- Update these thresholds based on empirical evidence: default values are intentionally conservative.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Should affinity windows be extended for mobile sessions when we open breakers? (tradeoff: UX vs. containment).
- Should we surface a per-customer override to pin traffic to degraded regions (for enterprise customers with dedicated capacity)? Current plan: enterprise customers on Dedicated may get bypass via entitlement flag; need security review.
- Run a canary experiment for 2 weeks with auto-open enabled for eu-west-1 to tune thresholds (PLAT-927).

References and quick links
-------------------------
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Routing+Design
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4389
- Incident tracker: PLAT-1021

Notes to self
-------------
- Keep this short; link to fuller runbook once we fold in infra playbooks for node autoscaling and disk pressure.
- Share with SRE rotation for feedback before marking final.
